companions.name: OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421 B
companions.description: The secondary star of the eclipsing binary OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421, 2.85 solar masses and 23.8 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 102.834 days.

radius.source: Secondary radius (solar radii) 23.8 +/- 0.2, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G)

mass.source: Secondary mass (solar masses) 2.85 +/- 0.02, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G)

temperature.source: Secondary log Teff 3.701 +/- 0.008, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G): 5023 K

orbit.source: OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421: P 102.8984 d and primary-eclipse time HJD 2452818.913 (the 2014 ephemeris, arXiv:1311.2340, with its observed period); i 88.05 degrees (arXiv:2010.08754, Table 3, column $i$ (deg)); e 0 (circular). HJD is taken as BJD_TDB (under a minute apart); at the primary eclipse the secondary is in front, the component these papers call primary being the one eclipsed at phase 0. Separation from Kepler's third law with DEBCat's masses

text.card: The secondary star of OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421, a pair that eclipse each other every 102.834 days.
text.introduction: It has 2.85 solar masses and 23.8 solar radii; its partner has 2.72 and 17.7, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), OGLE-SMC-ECL-1421: Mass, Radius and Period, from Graczyk et al. (2020ApJ...904...13G)
